meta.title: "Everyone does it" — Why can't your child say no? | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to recognise peer pressure and make their own choices — without fear of being left out. Game-based learning for kids 10–16.

hero.headline: "Everyone does it!" — does your child too?
hero.subheadline: They don't agree because they want to. They agree because they're afraid to stand out. It's time to teach them to make their own choice.

media.alt: A child surrounded by peers, trying not to stand out

pain.title: Peer pressure works automatically — and kids don't even notice
pain.body:
In the classroom, in group chats, on the playground — someone says "everyone does it" and your child starts to doubt themselves. Even when something inside tells them: "this doesn't feel right."

This isn't bad behaviour or weakness. It's social pressure manipulation — it works by exploiting the fear of being rejected. Children don't see it because no one ever explained how it works.

Kids who can't recognise group pressure conform — even at their own expense. They stay silent when they should say no, and do things they don't want to do just to stay in the group.

solution.title: "Sila Slova" — a detective drama that teaches critical thinking
solution.body: 50 episodes, 13 critical thinking lessons. Your child plays — but is actually learning to protect themselves.
bullets: 🔍 Recognises "everyone does it" as a manipulation tactic
🧠 Learns to think independently, not just follow the crowd
💬 Can calmly say no — without conflict or guilt
🛡️ Knows their own values and won't break under group pressure

social_proof.quote: "Everyone does it" doesn't work on my daughter anymore. For her, that's no longer enough reason to say yes.
social_proof.author: Natalia, mum of 11-year-old Alina

faq.q: Is this a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at once. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 10–16 year olds. At this age, children are receptive to new thinking patterns and are still forming their views.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
